rationale: I read the complete held EO 11943 (41 FR 47213, Oct. 28, 1976): one paragraph, issued 'to correct a typographical error', that amends the Section 4103 Schedule line for Director of Nursing Service in Schedule 3 of EO 11941 of Oct. 1, 1976 by changing '2,611*' to '52,611*'. Its whole operative content is an edit of a pay-schedule entry inside EO 11941; it has no standing text of its own. I read the operative secs. 1-5 of held EO 11941 (the Oct. 1, 1976 pay adjustment; Schedule 3 = Veterans Administration Department of Medicine and Surgery, which carries the Director of Nursing Service line) and held EO 12010 (42 FR 52365, Sept. 30, 1977): sec. 1(c) adopts a new Schedule 3 for the same VA pay system, sec. 3 makes the adjustments effective Oct. 1, 1977 (uniformed services) or the first applicable pay period on or after that date (all others), and sec. 4 'Superseded Orders. Executive Order No. 11941 of October 1, 1976, is superseded.' EO 12010 does not name EO 11943, so the ending is by supersession of the one instrument it amends, not an express revocation; I say so openly. No savings clause appears in EO 12010 or EO 11943, and the corrected figure had no function once EO 11941's Schedule 3 stopped operating. Partial scope: EO 11943 amends nothing else (no other order, no standing delegation). Earlier endings: EO 11943 has no own term or sunset, and the only other instruments naming EO 11941 in the held corpus are EO 12010 and EO 11943 (EO 9617 is an unrelated mention), so nothing superseded EO 11941 before EO 12010. D6 (later events that ended or changed the clause): the history holds one candidate event (OFR 'Superseded by: EO 12010', Sept. 28, 1977) and one empty 1989 snapshot; nothing amends, revives, extends or re-delegates EO 11943 after 1977 and EO 12010 is not itself shown to be revived. The OFR note agrees with my reading but is a lead; the basis is the held text of EO 12010 sec. 4 read against EO 11943's target. Provisional NO hypothesis only; the first-end date is not asserted.
